VIII TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Training - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky 
shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 initial pilot training course approximately 
ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual Flight Rules ("VFR") transition segment and, 
as required, an Instrument Flight Rules ("IFR") transition segment. Each of the segments is 
programmed to provide emphasis on helicopter familiarization, classroom instruction on 
systems operation and instruction in both the S-76 Simulator and the S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In 
addition, each Buyer pilot will receive two and one half (2.5) hours of flight with an instructor 
pilot. 
Each Buyer pilot must have a current U.S. commercial helicopter certificate or 
equivalent, and for the IFR segment, each Buyer pilot must have a current commercial 
certificate helicopter instrument rating, or equivalent. All flight training shall be conducted on 
the Deluxe Executive Helicopter to be delivered hereunder, following acceptance by the Buyer 
and transfer of title to the Buyer. 
2. Initial Maintenance or Electrical Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer 
mechanics an initial S-76 maintenance training course approximately fifteen (15) days in 
duration or, at Buyer's option, an S-76 electrical training course approximately ten (10) days in 
duration. Either course includes inspection and maintenance troubleshooting and use of a 
maintenance trainer. Each mechanic must have background experience in one or more of the 
following categories: 
certified (by the FAA or by an equivalent airworthiness authority) 
airframe mechanic with one (1) year practical experience as a rated aircraft mechanic: one (1) 
year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military helicopter; or three (3) 
years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft mechanic. 
3. Engine Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3)Buyer mechanics, an engine 
maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately five 
(5) days in duration.

HELICOPTER CONFIGURATION 
The following items of standard and optional equipment as described below, which have been 
selected by the Buyer, shall be installed on the Helicopter to be delivered under the Agreement. 
Part 1: 
BASELINE AIRCRAFT 
Features of the S-76C++ Aircraft: 
Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated main rotor system 
with dual controls. 
Cockpit  - An Integrated Instrument Display System (IIDS), with an easy to upgrade avionics package. 
There is a Bleed Air Heating Defogging system and dual windshield wipers. The Pilot and Copilot 
seats come with a five point Restraint system. 
Cabin - A large cabin that can be configured for four different missions and a 38 cubic foot baggage 
compartment 
Other - Retractable landing gear, and 281 gallons of usable fuel 
Baseline Avionics Package Includes: 
Collins Proline II: Dual Collins VHF 22A Comms and VIR 32 Nays, single ADF 462 ADF, TDR 90 
Transponder, DME 42 DME with IND 42A Indicator, ALT 55B Radio Altimeter with Expanded Scale 
ALI 55A Indicator.
Honeywell EFIS/DAFCS: 4-Tube Honeywell EDZ 756 EFTS with 5" x 6" Indicators Displaying Airspeed, 
Altitude and Vertical Speed. Dual Litef AHRS, Dual Penny and Giles Air Data Computers, Dual 
Honeywell Digital SPZ 7600 Automatic Flight Control System. Altitude Alert. 
Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC Generator. Dual 
375 VA Static Inverters. Avionics and EFTS Master Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance jacks, one in 
the cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 45° pedestal mounted ICS 
foot switches, three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-around cord and two 30-foot walk-around 
cords, Cabin PA/Chime System, and a Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 CVR, 3' Backup 
Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-335O Standby Attitude Indicator with Nay1/Nav2 Select, ELT 
406-NHM w/ Satellite Frequency, Electric Door Locks - Cabin. Single Action Door Release. 
Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440. Windshield Washer System, Heated 
Glass Windshields, and Engine Inlet Barrier Filter

Sikorsky shall furnish or offer to the Buyer certain publications under this paragraph for use by

Executive Helicopter at no additional cost to the Buyer. In addition, the Buyer may elect to 
receive S-76 Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETMs) contained on one (1) CD-ROM 
computer disk and/or via Internet access from a Sikorsky-provided web site for accessing the 
information contained in the S-76 Maintenance Manual, Illustrated Parts Catalog and 
Airworthiness Limitations and Inspection Requirements Manuals (Chapters 4 and 5). The 
IETMs shall be subject to Sikorsky's standard IETM software license agreement terms. The 
Buyer also shall receive all revisions to the Sikorsky IETMs for three (3) years after delivery of

VIII - TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Training - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky 
shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 initial pilot training course approximately 
ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual Flight Rules ("VFR") transition segment and, 
as required, an Instrument Flight Rules ("IFR") transition segment. Each of the segments is 
programmed to provide emphasis on helicopter familiarization, classroom instruction on 
systems operation and instruction in both the S-76 Simulator and the S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In 
addition, each Buyer pilot will receive two and one half (2.5) hours of flight with an instructor 
pilot. 
Each Buyer pilot must have a current U.S. commercial helicopter certificate or 
equivalent, and for the IFR segment, each Buyer pilot must have a current commercial 
certificate helicopter instrument rating, or equivalent. All flight training shall be conducted on 
the Deluxe Executive Helicopter to be delivered hereunder, following acceptance by the Buyer 
and transfer of title to the Buyer. 
2. Initial Maintenance or Electrical Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer 
mechanics an initial S-76 maintenance training course approximately fifteen (15) days in 
duration or, at Buyer's option, an S-76 electrical training course approximately ten (10) days in 
duration. Either course includes inspection and maintenance troubleshooting and use of a 
maintenance trainer. Each mechanic must have background experience in one or more of the 
following categories: 
certified (by the FAA or by an equivalent airworthiness authority) 
airframe mechanic with one (1) year practical experience as a rated aircraft mechanic; one (1) 
year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military helicopter; or three (3) 
years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft mechanic. 
3. Engine Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3)Buyer mechanics, an engine 
maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately five 
(5) days in duration.

HELICOPTER CONFIGURATION 
The following items of standard and optional equipment as described below, which have been 
selected by the Buyer, shall be installed on the Helicopter to be delivered under the Agreement. 
Part 1: 
BASELINE AIRCRAFT 
Features of the S-76C++ Aircraft: 
Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated main rotor system 
with dual controls. 
Cockpit  - An Integrated Instrument Display System (IIDS), with an easy to upgrade avionics package. 
There is a Bleed Air Heating Defogging system and dual windshield wipers. The Pilot and Copilot 
seats come with a five point Restraint system. 
Cabin — A large cabin that can be configured for four different missions and a 38 cubic foot baggage 
compartment 
Other  - Retractable landing gear, and 281 gallons of usable fuel 
Baseline Avionics Package Includes: 
Collins Proline II: Dual Collins VHF 22A Comms and VIR 32 Nays, single AOF 462 ADF, TDR 90 
Transponder, DME 42 DME with IND 42A Indicator, ALT 55B Radio Altimeter with Expanded Scale 
ALI 55A Indicator. 
Honeywell EFIS/DAFCS: 4-Tube Honeywell EDZ 756 EFIS with 5" x 6" Indicators Displaying Airspeed. 
Altitude and Vertical Speed, Dual Litef AHRS, Dual Penny and Giles Air Data Computers, Dual 
Honeywell Digital SPZ 7600 Automatic Flight Control System, Altitude Alert. 
Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC Generator, Dual 
375 VA Static Inverters. Avionics and EFIS Master Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance jacks, one in 
the cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 45° pedestal mounted ICS 
foot switches, three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-around cord and two 30-foot walk-around 
cords, Cabin PA/Chime System, and a Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 CVR, 3' Backup 
Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-335O Standby Attitude Indicator with maviimay2 select. ELT 
406-NHM w/ Satellite Frequency. Electric Door Locks — Cabin, Single Action Door Release, 
Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440, Windshield Washer System, Heated 
Glass Windshields, and Engine Inlet Barrier Filter

DESCRIPTION OF SALE 
1. Sale - Sikorsky shall sell and deliver to the Buyer, and the Buyer shall purchase from 
Sikorsky, the Quantity of one new Sikorsky Model S.-76C Helicopters with new 
Turbomeca 2S2 engines (known as the S-76C4-9 and equipped with the items of 
additional equipment specified In Exhibit A, Part 1 (the "Helicopter"). In addition, 
Sikorsky shall sell and perform the Completion Services for Buyer and Buyer shall 
purchase the Completion Services on the Helicopter, which will then be equipped with 
the items of additional cquipmait specified in Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, during the 
performance of the Completion Services, the configuration items specified in Annex 1 to 
Exhibit A shall be removed from the Helicopter and retained as property of Sikorsky. 
These configuration items shall be either deleted or replaced by the customized options 
chosen by Buyer in Exhibit A, Part 2 as part of the Completion Services 
2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for 
acceptance at the Sikorsky designated facility In Connecticut (the "Designated Facility") 
on the Scheduled Presentation Dates. Upon Buyer's request for a demonstration flight of 
the Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight at the Designated Facility 
during such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (I) hour in duration or 
longer as may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is 
conditioned upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy 
condition with all flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has 
been manufactured in accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the 
Helicopter has no damage, corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Tale Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall 
evidence Its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter 
Acceptance. Upon Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and 
payment of the Baseline Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section M.I.6., Sikorsky 
shall transfer title to Buyer at the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky 
shall provide to Buyer a FAA Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty

configuration and Helicopter Unit Price of the Replacement Helicopter required due to 
obsolescence, FAA requirements, or as a result of changes in the manufacture of the 
Helicopter), or (ii) terminate this Agreement. Buyer shall notify Sikorsky of its decision 
within fifteen (15) days of receipt by Buyer of written notice from Sikorsky of the loss or 
destruction of or damage beyond economic repair to the Helicopter, which notice shall 
include the projected delivery date of the Replacement Helicopter.

with the Honeywell MARK XXII Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System ("EPGWS") and 
the Universal 120 Cockpit voice data recorder. The EGPWS provides a real-time situational 
awareness of surrounding terrain and obstacles in relation to the aircraft's altitude and flight path. 
The system is designed to visually and aurally alert the flight crew to potential trouble ahead.

Subject 
Air Ghistaine Cell phone installations 
Mike, 
below is a draft email to Air Ghislaine to explain why we ca&t install a cell phone in the cockpit of their S-76 in the way 
we had discussed with them. Sorry this took so long....flve had a lot of discussion/negotiation/etc. with Keystone to make 
sure we have a solid solution. Please review, modify as appropriate and send to the customer so we can get their OK and 
have Keystone quote a new solution. 
Thanks 
Tom 
Below are the cell phone and iPod options currently contracted for the Air Ghislaine S-76Ot. configuration, including some 
comments and recommendations about these. We would appreciate your response to these so we can update the 
quotation and complete design work. Please provide your approval of the recommendations, or an alternate 
recommendation. 
32001 Cellular Phone Base and Charger 
Surface mount in cockpit or cabin area, a customer supplied cellular phone charging base. Installation includes: surface 
mounting of phone base to cockpit floor or bulkhead; 28 vdc to 14 vdc voltage converter, circuit breaker; mounting 
hardware; aircraft wiring; etc. Custom built-in mounting of charger base is available at an additional charge and must be 
quoted on an individual basis. Cellular phones are not permitted to be used while airborne. 
Comments: At the configuration meeting, we understood your desire to have the cockpit cell phone integrated into the 
cockpit audio control panels in order to enable direct use of the cell phone through the cockpit headsets. After further 
investigation of this type of installation, our completion center, Keystone Helicopter, provided the rationale below for 
avoiding this approach: 
Keystone Statement: 
Keystone Helicopter Corporation (KHC) no longer accepts work to modify existing aircraft or new aircraft with 
integrated cell phones into the cockpit. Historically mobile phones have been installed in the cockpit and integrated 
into the ICS system with the understanding that system can not be used inflight due to FCC and FM guidelines. 
Recent guidelines within the FM have forced a review of these installations as to the environmental qualifications of 
the equipment and a failure hazard assessment of the install. Typically, customers request their current phones which 
rarely meet any environmental qualification (i.e. DO-160, mil-std 810...) or have been evaluated for their MTBF in a 
helicopter environment. Failure of the system may directly effect other cockpit flight equipment and increase pilot 
workload. 
Recommendation: Keep the cell phone base and charger as currently In the contracted configuration (described above in 
32001). The ability to make cell phone calls through the headsets can be achieved by purchase of a commercially 
available headset-cell phone interface unit.

90008 Cell Phone interface in cabin to allow cell phone to be plugged in and communication enabled through 
cabin Bose headsets 
Comments: Will function as described in option title above. FAA regulations prohibit use of cell phones while airborne, 
therefore the cabin cell phone interface will be disabled in flight through a link to the weight-on-wheels switch. 
90009 Audio input jack in cabin for Ipod type device. Entertainment audio to be heard In all cabin Bose headsets. 
No other controls, volume controlled via IPod device 
Comments: No issues. 
90010 Audio Input Jack in cockpit for Ipod type device. Entertainment audio to be heard in both cockpit Bose 
headsets only. No other controls, volume controlled via IPod device 
Comments: No issues.

helicopter familiarization, classroom instruction on systems operation and instruction in

receive two and one half (2.5) ;touts of flight with an instructor pilot. Each Buyer pilot

instrument rating, or equivalent All flight training shall be conducted on the Deluxe

The change of the corporate name of Air Ghislaine, Inc. was a change of name only; it did 
nothing to effect the valid and cxi icing legal identity, existence or status of this corporate entity. 
It did not in any way change or modify any of the corporate entity's rights or obligations under 
any existing agreements that the corporate entity entered into prior to the name change, including 
without limitation, that certain 5-76OI-) New Helicopter Sales Agreement between Assignor and 
Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation dived on or about December 17, 2007, as amended (the "Sales 
Agreement"), related to the sale of that certain S-76C+-f helicopter with manufacturer's serial 
number 760750. Thus, the rights and obligations of this corporate entity under the Sales 
Agreement remain in MI force and effect after the name change to the same extent that they 
existed immediately prior to the tame change, with the exception that moving forward any and 
all agreements, amendments, designations, acceptances, communications or other documents to 
be addressed to or executed by this corporate entity in connection with the Sales Agreement shall 
he addressed to or executed by the corporate entity in the name of Shmitka Air, Inc. with the 
same effect as if they were addressed to or executed in the name of Air Ghislaine, Inc.

Subject: Notification of Name Change 
Dear Chris, 
Please be advised that on or about February 12, 2010, Air Ghislaine, Inc. filed an amendment to 
its Certificate of Incorporation with the Delaware Secretary of State, changing its name from 
"Air Ghislaine, Inc." to "Shmitka Air, Inc." Because the Secretary of State was closed on 
February I I, 2010, when the document was submitted to the corporate service company a 
request was made for the filing to be effective on February 11, 2010. In any event, this corporate 
name change is now effective. 
The change of the corporate name of Air Ghislaine, Inc. was a change of name only; it did 
nothing to effect the valid and existing legal identity, existence or status of this corporate entity. 
It did not in any way change or modify any of the corporate entity's rights or obligations under 
any existing agreements that the corporate entity entered into prior to the name change, including 
without limitation, that certain S-76C++ New Helicopter Sales Agreement between Assignor and 
Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation dated on or about December 17, 2007, as amended (the "Sales 
Agreement"), related to the sale of that certain S-76C++ helicopter with manufacturer's serial 
number 760750. Thus, the rights rind obligations of this corporate entity under the Sales 
Agreement remain in MI force and effect after the name change to the same extent that they 
existed immediately prior to the name change, with the exception that moving forward any and 
all agreements, amendments, designations, acceptances, communications or other documents to 
be addressed to or executed by this corporate entity in connection with the Sales Agreement shall 
be addressed to or executed by the corporate entity in the name of Shmitka Air, Inc. with the 
same effect as if they were addressed to or executed in the name of Air Ghislaine, Inc. 
Sincerely 
Darren K. lndyke

2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for

may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is conditioned 
upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy condition with all 
flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has been manufactured in 
accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the Helicopter has no damage, 
corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Title Trans for - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section 
Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helicopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut, to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center") via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion 
Services. 
4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any person to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registra ion of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and at Buyer's expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance Dn the Helicopter in connection therewith. 
5. Risk of Loss - Sikorsky shall have risk of loss of the Helicopter, subsequent to the transfer of 
title through Buyer's acceptance of the Completion Services. In the event that the Helicopter 
is damaged or the functionality is in any way compromised during the conduct of the 
Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the Completion Services, to 
repair such damage or restore such functionality to as good condition as new. Buyer agrees 
that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid directly to Sikorsky. In the event

Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certification by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under 
Federal Aviation Regulation ("=AR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate H1NE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, -Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcrafl". Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificate PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FM approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility Nholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA.

VII- TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Initial Pilot Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 initial pilot training 
course approximately ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual Flight Rules ("VFR") 
transition segment and, as required, an Instrument Flight Rules ("IFR") transition segment. 
Each of the segments is programmed to provide emphasis on helicopter familiarization, 
classroom instruction on syster is operation and instruction in both the S-76 Simulator and the 
S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In addition, each Buyer pilot will receive two and one half (2.5) hours of 
flight with an instructor pilot. 
Each Buyer pilot must have a current U.S. commercial 
helicopter certificate or equiva ent, and for the IFR segment, each Buyer pilot must have a 
current commercial certificate helicopter instrument rating, or equivalent. All flight training 
shall be conducted on the Deluxe Executive Helicopter to be delivered hereunder, following 
acceptance by the Buyer and hansfer of title to the Buyer. 
2. Initial Maintenance or Electrical Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer 
mechanics an initial S-76 maintenance training course approximately fifteen (15) days in 
duration or, at Buyer's option, an S-76 electrical training course approximately ten (10) days 
in duration. Either course includes inspection and maintenance troubleshooting and use of a 
maintenance trainer. Each mi:chanic must have background experience in one or more of 
the following categories: certified (by the FAA or by an equivalent airworthiness authority) 
airframe mechanic with one (1) year practical experience as a rated aircraft mechanic; one (1) 
year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military helicopter; or three (3) 
years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft mechanic. 
3. Engine Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer mechanics, an engine 
maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately five 
(5) days in duration.

BASELINE AIRCRAFT

Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Argo' 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated main rotor system with

Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC Generator, Dual 
Static Inverters, Avionics and EFIS Mastin Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance jacks, one in the 
cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 45° pedestal mounted ICS foot switches, 
three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-around cord and two 30-foot walk-around cords, Cabin 
PA/Chime System, and a Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 CVR, r Backup 
Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-3350 Standby Attitude Indicator with Nav1/Nav2 Select, ELT 406-NHM 
w/ Satellite Frequency, Electric Door Locks — Cabin, Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440, Windshield Washer System, Heated Glass 
Windshields, and Engine Inlet Barrier Filer

Additional Requirement for Completion Center 
The completion center is responsible for ensuring the documentation that is delivered to the 
customer reflects the delivered configuration. The documents to be delivered with the helicopter 
include, but are not limited to: Pilot (luides for cockpit equipment, Electrical Load Analysis Report, 
Weight & Balance Report, 1p and 4p Vibration Report, Aircraft Equipment Inventory Listing, 
Certificate of Airworthiness, Return to Service, CVR/FDR Reasonability Check Report, Option Data 
Package for continued airworthiness for all equipment installed by the Completion Center which is 
not covered in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. 
All Transponders, ELT's and other programmable devices are to be programmed with appropriate 
information to be provided by Customer. 
All aircraft equipment Software and databases are to be updated/loaded by the completion center 
prior to delivery. Completion Center will also submit a subscription application to each supplier for a 
minimum of 12 months software/database subscription. Additionally, all data transfer cables and 
special equipment necessary to perform these functions will be provided to the customer.

DESCRIPTION OF SALE 
1. Sale - Sikorsky shall sell and deliver to the Buyer, and the Buyer shall purchase from 
Sikorsky, the Quantity of one new Sikorsky Model S-76C Helicopters with new Turbomeca 
2S2 engines (known as the S-76C++) and equipped with the items of additional equipment 
specified in Exhibit A, Part 1 (the -Helicopter). In addition, Sikorsky shall sell and perform the 
Completion Services for Buyer and Buyer shall purchase the Completion Services on the 
Helicopter, which will then be equipped with the items of additional equipment specified in 
Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe Executive Helicopter). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary 
contained herein, during the inrformance of the Completion Services, the configuration items 
specified in Annex 1 to Exhibit A shall be removed from the Helicopter and retained as 
property of Sikorsky. These configuration items shall be either deleted or replaced by the

upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy condition with all 
flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has been manufactured in

3. Acceptance and Title Transfor - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section III.1.b., Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helcopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut, to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center") via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion 
Services. 
4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any person to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registraion of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and at Buyer's expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance on the Helicopter in connection therewith.

Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certificaticn by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under 
Federal Aviation Regulation (TAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate H1 NE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft'. Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificate PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility inholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA.

Helicopter is destroyed during :he period of such flight tests, such destruction arising from any

Additional Requirement for Completion Center 
The completion center is responsible for ensuring the documentation that is delivered to the 
customer reflects the delivered configuration. The documents .to be delivered with the helicopter 
include, but are not limited to: Pilot guides for cockpit equipment, Electrical Load Analysis Report, 
Weight & Balance Report, 1p and 4p Vibration Report, Aircraft Equipment Inventory Listing, 
Certificate of Airworthiness, Return to Service, CVR/FDR Reasonability Check Report, Option Data 
Package for continued airworthiness for all equipment installed by the Completion Center which is 
not covered in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. 
All Transponders, ELT's and other programmable devices are to be programmed with appropriate 
information to be provided by Customer. 
All aircraft equipment Software and databases are to be updated/loaded by the completion center 
prior to delivery. Completion Center will also submit a subscription application to each supplier for a 
minimum of 12 months software/database subscription. Additionally, all data transfer cables and 
special equipment necessary to perform these functions will be provided to the customer. 
This 
includes, but is not limited to: EGPWS FMS, Garmin GMX 200. 
Aircraft is to be flown into retorque window and all retorques are to be accomplished prior to delivery. 
Helicopter will be delivered with sufficient flight time available to enable ferry flight to customer's 
home base without need for retorque or scheduled maintenance or inspections.

DESCRIPTION OF SALE 
1. Sale - Sikorsky shall sell and deliver to the Buyer, and the Buyer shall purchase from 
Sikorsky, the Quantity of one new Sikorsky Model S-76C Helicopters with new Turbomeca 
2S2 engines (known as the S-76C++) and equipped with the items of additional equipment 
specified in Exhibit A, Part 1 (the "Helicopter"). In addition, Sikorsky shall sell and perform the 
Completion Services for Buyer and Buyer shall purchase the Completion Services on the 
Helicopter, which will then be equipped with the items of additional equipment specified in 
Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe Executive Helicopter"). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary 
contained herein, during the performance of the Completion Services, the configuration items 
specified in Annex 1 to Exhibit A shall be removed from the Helicopter and retained as 
property of Sikorsky. These configuration items shall be either deleted or replaced by the 
customized options chosen by Euyer in Exhibit A, Part 2 as part of the Completion Services. 
2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for 
acceptance at the Sikorsky designated facility in Connecticut (the "Designated Facility") on the 
Scheduled Presentation Dates 
Upon Buyer's request for a demonstration flight of the 
Helicopter. Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight at the Designated Facility during 
such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or longer as

3. Acceptance and Title Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section lll.1.b., Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FM 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helicopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut, to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center) via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion Services. 
• 4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any person to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registration of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and at Buyer's expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance on the Helicopter in connection therewith. 
5. Risk of Loss — Sikorsky shall have risk of loss of the Helicopter, subsequent to the transfer of 
title through Buyer's acceptance of the Completion Services. In the event that the Helicopter 
is damaged or the functionality is in any way compromised during the conduct of the 
Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the Completion Services, to 
repair such damage or restore iiuch functionality to as good condition as new. Buyer agrees 
that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid directly to Sikorsky. In the event 
the Helicopter is lost or destroyed or damaged beyond economic repair at any time prior to 
Buyer's acceptance, Buyer shall have the right to either (i) purchase the next available S-76 
C++ Helicopter in Sikorsky's production sequence (the'Replacement Helicopter) on the 
same terms and conditions as set forth in this Agreement, (however Sikorsky reserves the 
right to make changes in the Exhibit A configuration and Helicopter Unit Price of the 
Replacement Helicopter required due to obsolescence, FAA requirements, or as a result of

Thereafter, upon the receipt of the Completion Services Final Payment pursuant to Article Ill. 
1.d. below, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FM return to service certification and the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter shall then tie at Buyer's risk.

VI - HELICOPTER RELATED PROVISIONS 
1. 
Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has been 
granted Type Certification by thy; U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under Federal 
Aviation Regulation ("FAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 as 
defined by Type Certificate H1NE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft". Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production CertificatE PC-105 granted in accordance with 'FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA appoval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility wholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA. 
2. Special Flight Tests - Flight te:;t work required for prototyping of any components or system 
detailed in ParagraphVll.5 below, functional checkout, or qualification of any additional 
equipment contracted may be performed by Sikorsky on the Helicopter and the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter prior to title transfer thereto or final delivery thereof, respectively, to the 
Buyer. The delivery of the Helicopter or the Deluxe Executive Helicopter may be delayed to 
the extent necessary to accomplish the flight test work objectives without any liability on the 
part of Sikorsky for any such delay. 
In the event the Helicopter or Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter is destroyed during the period of such flight tests, such destruction arising from any 
cause whatsoever, Sikorsky skill be under no obligation to furnish a substitute Helicopter or 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter but shall rather be relieved of all obligations with respect to the 
delivery of such Helicopter or Deluxe Executive Helicopter so destroyed, except that Sikorsky 
or the insurance company shall promptly refund to Buyer all amounts theretofore paid by 
Buyer with respect to the purchase price thereof.

VII- TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Initial Pilot Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 initial pilot training 
course approximately ten (10) !Jays in duration, consisting of a Visual Flight Rules ("VFR") 
transition segment and, as required. an Instrument Flight Rules ("IFR") transition segment. 
Each of the segments is programmed to provide emphasis on helicopter familiarization, 
classroom instruction on systems operation and instruction in both the S-76 Simulator and the 
S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In addition, each Buyer pilot will receive two and one half (2.5) hours of 
flight with an instructor pilot. Each Buyer pilot must have a current U.S. commercial helicopter 
certificate or equivalent, and for the IFR segment, each Buyer pilot must have a current 
commercial certificate helicopter instrument rating, or equivalent. All flight training shall be

Part 1: 
BASELINE AIRCRAFT 
Features of the S-76C++ Aircraft Code 0102: 
Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated main rotor system with 
dual controls. 
Cockpit  —An Integrated Instrument Display System (IIDS), with an easy to upgrade avionics package. There 
is a Bleed Air Heating Defogging system a•nd dual windshield wipers. The Pilot and Copilot seats come with a 
five point Restraint system. 
Cabin — A large cabin that can be configured for four different missions and a 38 cubic foot baggage 
compartment 
Other — Retractable landing gear, and 281 gallons of usable fuel 
Baseline Avionics Package Includes: 
Collins Proline II: Dual Collins VHF 22A C:omms and VIR 32 Nays, single ADF 462 ADF, TDR 90 
Transponder, DME 42 DME with IND 42A Indicator, ALT 1000 Radio Altimeter with Expanded Scale ALI 55A 
Indicator. 
Honeywell EFIS/DAFCS: 4-Tube Honeywell EDZ 756 EFIS with 5" x 6" Indicators Displaying Airspeed, 
Altitude and Vertical Speed, Dual Litef AHRS, Dual Penny and Giles Air Data Computers, Dual Honeywell 
Digital SPZ 7600 Automatic Flight Control System, Altitude Alert. 
Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC Generator, Dual Static 
Inverters, Avionics and EFIS Master Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance jacks, one in the 
cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 45° pedestal mounted ICS foot switches, 
three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-around cord and two 30-foot walk-around cords, Cabin 
PA/Chime System, and a Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 CVR, 3" Backup 
Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-335() Standby Attitude Indicator with Nav1/Nav2 Select, ELT 406•NHM 
w/ Satellite Frequency, Electric Door Lock t. — Cabin, Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440, Windshield Washer System, Heated Glass 
Windshields, and Engine Inlet Barrier Filter

Additional Requirement for Completion Center 
The completion center is responsibla for ensuring the documentation that is delivered to the 
customer reflects the delivered configuration. The documents to be delivered with the helicopter 
include, but are not limited to: Pilot guides for cockpit equipment, Electrical Load Analysis Report, 
Weight & Balance Report, 1p and 4p Vibration Report, Aircraft Equipment Inventory Listing, 
Certificate of Airworthiness, Return to Service, CVR/FDR Reasonability Check Report, Option Data 
Package for continued airworthiness lor all equipment installed by the Completion Center which is 
not covered in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. 
All Transponders, ELT's and other programmable devices are to be programmed with appropriate 
information to be provided by Customer.

upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy condition with all 
flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has been manufactured in 
accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the Helicopter has no damage. 
corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Title Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section III.1.b., Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. 
Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helicopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut. to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center") via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion 
Services. 
4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any person to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registra ton of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and Et Buyer's expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance Dr) the Helicopter in connection therewith.

Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the Completion Services, to 
repair such damage or restore such functionality to as good condition as new. Buyer agrees 
that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid directly to Sikorsky. In the event

VI HELICOPTER RELATED PROVISIONS 
1. 
Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certification by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (°FAA") under 
Federal Aviation Regulation ("FAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate HINE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft" 
Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificata PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility wholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA. 
2. Special Flight Tests - Flight test work required for prototyping of any components or system 
detailed in ParagraphVII.5 below, functional checkout, or qualification of any additional 
equipment contracted may be performed by Sikorsky on the Helicopter and the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter prior to title transfer thereto or final delivery thereof, respectively, to the 
Buyer. The delivery of the Helicopter or the Deluxe Executive Helicopter may be delayed to 
the extent necessary to accomplish the flight test work objectives without any liability on the 
part of Sikorsky for any such delay. In the event the Helicopter or Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter is destroyed during the period of such flight tests, such destruction arising from any 
cause whatsoever, Sikorsky shall be under no obligation to furnish a substitute Helicopter or 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter but shall rather be relieved of all obligations with respect to the 
delivery of such Helicopter or Deluxe Executive Helicopter so destroyed, except that Sikorsky 
or the insurance company shall promptly refund to Buyer all amounts theretofore paid by 
Buyer with respect to the purchase price thereof.

airframe mechanic with one (1) year practical experience as a rated aircraft mechanic; one (1)

years general experience as a :ommercial or military aircraft mechanic.

maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately five

Additional Requirement for Completion Center 
The completion center is responsible for ensuring the documentation that is delivered to the 
customer reflects the delivered configuration. The documents to be delivered with the helicopter 
include, but are not limited to: Pilot guides for cockpit equipment, Electrical Load Analysis Report, 
Weight & Balance Report, 1p and 4p Vibration Report, Aircraft Equipment Inventory Listing, 
Certificate of Airworthiness, Return to Service, CVR/FDR Reasonability Check Report, Option Data 
Package for continued airworthiness for all equipment installed by the Completion Center which is 
not covered in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. 
All Transponders, ELT's and other programmable devices are to be programmed with appropriate 
information to be provided by Customer. 
All aircraft equipment Software and databases are to be updated/loaded by the completion center 
prior to delivery. Completion Center will also submit a subscription application to each supplier for a 
minimum of 12 months software/database subscription. Additionally, all data transfer cables and 
special equipment necessary to perform these functions will be provided to the customer. 
This 
includes, but is not limited to: EGPWS, FMS, Garmin GMX 200.

DESCRIPTION OF SALE 
1. Sale - Sikorsky shall sell and deliver to the Buyer, and the Buyer shall purchase from 
Sikorsky, the Quantity of one new Sikorsky Model S-76C Helicopters with new Turbomeca 
2S2 engines (known as the S-76C++) and equipped with the items of additional equipment 
specified in Exhibit A, Part 1 (the "Helicopter"). In addition, Sikorsky shall sell and perform the 
Completion Services for Buyer and Buyer shall purchase the Completion Services on the 
Helicopter, which will then be equipped with the items of additional equipment specified in 
Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe Executive Helicopter"). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary 
contained herein, during the performance of the Completion Services, the configuration items 
specified in Annex 1 to Exhibit A shall be removed from the Helicopter and retained as 
property of Sikorsky. These configuration items shall be either deleted or replaced by the 
customized options chosen by Buyer in Exhibit A, Part 2 as part of the Completion Services.

2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for 
acceptance at the Sikorsky designated facility in Connecticut (the "Designated Facility") on 
the Scheduled Presentation Dates. Upon Buyer's request for a demonstration flight of the 
Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight at the Designated Facility during 
such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or longer as 
may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is conditioned 
upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy condition with all 
flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has been manufactured in 
accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the Helicopter has no damage, 
corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Title Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section III.1.b., Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helicopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut, to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center") via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion 
Services. 
4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any person to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registration of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and at Buyer's expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance on the Helicopter in connection therewith. 
5. Risk of Loss - Sikorsky shall have risk of loss of the Helicopter, subsequent to the transfer of 
title through Buyer's acceptance of the Completion Services. In the event that the Helicopter 
is damaged or the functionality is in any way compromised during the conduct of the 
Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the Completion Services, to 
repair such damage or restore such functionality to as good condition as new. Buyer agrees 
that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid directly to Sikorsky. In the event

5. Presentation of Completion Services for Acceptance - Upon the completion of the 
Completion Services, the Deluxe Executive Helicopter shall be presented for technical 
acceptance of the work performed at the Completion Center on the Scheduled Presentation 
Date Completion Services. Upon Buyer's request for an inspection and demonstration flight 
of the Deluxe Executive Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight of the 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter, at the Completion Center during such inspection and 
presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or longer as may 
reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to accept the Deluxe Executive Helicopter is 
conditioned upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Completion Services have 
been satisfactorily completed and that the Helicopter as previously accepted by Buyer, is in 
airworthy condition with all systems functional and in proper working order and with no 
damage incurred. 
6. Acceptance of Completion Services - After the completion of the inspection, the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter shall be presented to Buyer for final acceptance of the Completion 
Services at the Designated Facility. Buyer shall evidence its acceptance of the Completion 
Services by executing a Certificate of Acceptance of the Completion Services (Exhibit C). 
Thereafter, upon the receipt of the Completion Services Final Payment pursuant to Article III. 
1.d. below, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA retum to service certification and the 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter shall then be at Buyer's risk.

VI - HELICOPTER RELATED PROVISIONS 
1. 
Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certification by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under 
Federal Aviation Regulation ("FAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate H1NE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft'. Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificate PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility wholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA. 
2. Special Flight Tests - Flight test work required for prototyping of any components or system 
detailed in ParagraphVll.5 below, functional checkout, or qualification of any additional 
equipment contracted may be performed by Sikorsky on the Helicopter and the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter prior to title transfer thereto or final delivery thereof, respectively, to the 
Buyer. The delivery of the Heicopter or the Deluxe Executive Helicopter may be delayed to 
the extent necessary to accomplish the flight test work objectives without any liability on the 
part of Sikorsky for any suct delay. 
In the event the Helicopter or Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter is destroyed during the period of such flight tests, such destruction arising from any 
cause whatsoever, Sikorsky shall be under no obligation to furnish a substitute Helicopter or 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter but shall rather be relieved of all obligations with respect to the 
delivery of such Helicopter or Deluxe Executive Helicopter so destroyed, except that Sikorsky 
or the insurance company shall promptly refund to Buyer all amounts theretofore paid by 
Buyer with respect to the purchase price thereof.

V. 
WARRANTIES 
Warranties - Sikorsky's warranties and Buyer's remedies are set forth in Exhibit B Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter Warranty. 
1. Engine Warranty- The engine manufacturer warranties and Buyer's remedies are set forth in 
Exhibit C. As a matter accommodation to Buyer Sikorsky shall obtain from the engine 
manufacturer, Turbomeca, a warranty extension of one year beyond the standard two years, 
for a total duration of three years or 1,000 flight hours as defined in paragraph 1.1 of Exhibit 
C, Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 Turboshaft Engine, that is attached hereto for reference. For the 
avoidance of doubt, the engine remains warranted by the engine manufacturer and all other 
terms and conditions of the engine manufacturer warranty shall remain unchanged.

Executive Helicopter at no additional cost to the Buyer. In addition, the Buyer may elect to 
receive S-76 Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETMs) contained on one (1) CD-ROM 
computer disk and/or via Internet access from a Sikorsky-provided web site for accessing the 
information contained in the S-76 Maintenance Manual, Illustrated Parts Catalog and 
Airworthiness Limitations and Inspection Requirements Manuals (Chapters 4 and 5). The 
IETMs shall be subject to Sikorsky's standard IETM software license agreement terms. The 
Buyer also shall receive all revisions to the Sikorsky IETMs for three (3) years after delivery of 
the Deluxe Executive Helicopter at no additional cost to the Buyer. In addition, Sikorsky shall 
provide one copy of the operational and maintenance manuals of options, system schematics 
for the Deluxe Executive Helicopter normally available from Sikorsky and aviation 
subcontractors.

The following items of standard and optional equipment as described below, which have been 
selected by the Buyer, shall be installed on the Helicopter to be delivered under the Agreement. 
Part 1: 
BASELINE AIRCRAFT 
Features of the S-76C++ Aircraft Code 0102: 
Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated main rotor system with 
dual controls. 
Cockpit — An Integrated Instrument Display System IDS), with an easy to upgrade avionics package. There 
is a Bleed Air Heating Defogging system and dual windshield wipers. The Pilot and Copilot seats come with a 
five point Restraint system. 
Cabin — A large cabin that can be configured for four different missions and a 38 cubic foot baggage 
compartment 
Other — Retractable landing gear, and 281 gallons of usable fuel 
Baseline Avionics Package Includes: 
Collins Proline II: Dual Collins VHF 22A Comms and VIR 32 Nays, single ADF 462 ADF, TDR 90 
Transponder, DME 42 DME with IND 42A Indicator, ALT 1000 Radio Altimeter with Expanded Scale ALI 55A 
Indicator. 
Honeywell EFIS/DAFCS: 4-Tube Honeywell EDZ 756 EFIS with 5" x 6" Indicators Displaying Airspeed, 
Altitude and Vertical Speed, Dual Litef AHRS, Dual Penny and Giles Air Data Computers, Dual Honeywell 
Digital SPZ 7600 Automatic Flight Control System, Altitude Alert. 
Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC Generator. Dual 
Static Inverters, Avionics and EFIS Master Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance jacks, one in the 
cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 45° pedestal mounted ICS foot switches, 
three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-around cord and two 30-foot walk-around cords, Cabin 
PA/Chime System, and a Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 CVR, r Backup 
Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-335D Standby Attitude Indicator with Nav1/Nav2 Select, ELT 406-NHM 
w/ Satellite Frequency, Electric Door Locks — Cabin, Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440, Windshield Washer System, Heated Glass 
Windshields, and Engine Inlet Barrier Filter

1. 
Type Design and Productior.' Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certification by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA') under 
Federal Aviation Regulation (WAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate H1 NE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft". Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificate PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility wholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA.

detailed in ParagraphVll.5 below, functional checkout, or qualification of any additional 
equipment contracted may be performed by Sikorsky on the Helicopter and the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter prior to title transfer thereto or final delivery thereof, respectively, to the 
Buyer. The delivery of the Helicopter or the Deluxe Executive Helicopter may be delayed to 
the extent necessary to accomplish the flight test work objectives without any liability on the 
part of Sikorsky for any suer' delay. 
In the event the Helicopter or Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter is destroyed during the period of such flight tests, such destruction arising from any 
cause whatsoever, Sikorsky shall be under no obligation to furnish a substitute Helicopter or 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter but shall rather be relieved of all obligations with respect to the 
delivery of such Helicopter or Deluxe Executive Helicopter so destroyed, except that Sikorsky 
or the insurance company shall promptly refund to Buyer all amounts theretofore paid by 
Buyer with respect to the purchase price thereof.

information to be provided by Customer.

DESCRIPTION OF SALE 
1. Sale - Sikorsky shall sell and deliver to the Buyer, and the Buyer shall purchase from 
Sikorsky, the Quantity of one new Sikorsky Model S-76C Helicopters with new Turbomeca 
2S2 engines (known as the S-76C++) and equipped with the items of additional equipment 
specified in Exhibit A, Part 1 (the -Helicopter"). In addition, Sikorsky shall sell and perform the 
Completion Services for Buyer and Buyer shall purchase the Completion Services on the 
Helicopter, which will then be equipped with the items of additional equipment specified in 
Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe E Kecutive Helicopter"). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary 
contained herein, during the performance of the Completion Services, the configuration items 
specified in Annex 1 to Exhibit A shall be removed from the Helicopter and retained as 
property of Sikorsky. These configuration items shall be either deleted or replaced by the 
customized options chosen by l3uyer in Exhibit A, Part 2 as part of the Completion Services.

2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for 
acceptance at the Sikorsky destgnated facility in Connecticut (the "Designated Facility") on 
the Scheduled Presentation Dates. Upon Buyer's request for a demonstration flight of the 
Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight at the Designated Facility during 
such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or longer as 
may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is conditioned 
upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy condition with all 
flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has been manufactured in 
accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the Helicopter has no damage, 
corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Title Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section III.1.b., Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helicopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut, to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center") via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion 
Services. 
4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any perion to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registration of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and at Buyer's expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance on the Helicopter in connection therewith. 
5. Risk of Loss — Sikorsky shall have risk of loss of the Helicopter, subsequent to the transfer of 
title through Buyer's acceptance of the Completion Services. In the event that the Helicopter 
is damaged or the functionality is in any way compromised during the conduct of the 
Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the Completion Services, to 
repair such damage or restore such functionality to as good condition as new. Buyer agrees 
that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid directly to Sikorsky. In the event

Deluxe Executive Helicopter shall then be at Buyer's risk.

VI - HELICOPTER RELATED PROVISIONS 
1. 
Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certification by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under 
Federal Aviation Regulation ("FAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate HINE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft". Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificate PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility wholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FM. 
2. Special Flight Tests - Flight test work required for prototyping of any components or system 
detailed in ParagraphVll.5 below, functional checkout, or qualification of any additional 
equipment contracted may be performed by Sikorsky on the Helicopter and the Deluxe

Buyer. The delivery of the Helicopter or the Deluxe Executive Helicopter may be delayed to 
the extent necessary to accomplish the flight test work objectives without any liability on the

Executive Helicopter Warranty.

Exhibit C. As a matter accommodation to Buyer Sikorsky shall obtain from the engine 
manufacturer, Turbomeca, a warranty extension of one year beyond the standard two years, 
for a total duration of three years or 1,000 flight hours as defined in paragraph 1.1 of Exhibit. 
C, Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 Turboshaft Engine, that is attached hereto for reference. For the 
avoidance of doubt, the engine remains warranted by the engine manufacturer and all other 
terms and conditions of the engine manufacturer warranty shall remain unchanged. 
VI - HELICOPTER RELATED PROVISIONS 
3. Publications - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, 
Sikorsky shall furnish or offer to the Buyer certain publications under this paragraph for use 
by the Buyer and its contractors in operating and supporting the Deluxe Executive Helicopter. 
Sikorsky shall provide the Buyer with two paper copies of the Pilot's Flight Operating Manual 
and one copy each of the Sikorsky Maintenance Manual, Illustrated Parts Catalog, Wiring 
Manual, Engine Operating and Maintenance Manual and Engine Illustrated Parts Breakdown, 
and all revisions to each Sikorsky manual for three (3) years after delivery of each Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter at no additional cost to the Buyer. In addition, the Buyer may elect to 
receive S-76 Interactive Electronic Technical Manuals (IETMs) contained on one (1) CD-ROM 
computer disk and/or via Internet access from a Sikorsky-provided web site for accessing the 
information contained in the S-76 Maintenance Manual, Illustrated Parts Catalog and 
Airworthiness Limitations and inspection Requirements Manuals (Chapters 4 and 5). The 
IETMs shall be subject to Sikorsky's standard IETM software license agreement terms. The 
Buyer also shall receive all revisions to the Sikorsky IETMs for three (3) years after delivery of 
the Deluxe Executive Helicopter at no additional cost to the Buyer. In addition, Sikorsky shall 
provide one copy of the operational and maintenance manuals of options, system schematics 
for the Deluxe Executive Helicopter normally available from Sikorsky and aviation 
subcontractors.

VII - TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Initial Pilot Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 initial pilot training 
course approximately ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual Flight Rules ("VFR") 
transition segment and, as required, an Instrument Flight Rules ("IFR") transition segment.

Each of the segments is programmed to provide emphasis on helicopter familiarization, 
classroom instruction on systems operation and instruction in both the S-76 Simulator and the 
S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In addition, each Buyer pilot will receive two and one half (2.5) hours of

Each Buyer pilot must have a current U.S. commercial 
helicopter certificate or equivalent, and for the IFR segment, each Buyer pilot must have a 
current commercial certificate helicopter instrument rating, or equivalent. All flight training 
shall be conducted on the Deluxe Executive Helicopter to be delivered hereunder, following 
acceptance by the Buyer and transfer of title to the Buyer. 
2. Initial Maintenance or Electrical Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer 
mechanics an initial S-76 maintenance training course approximately fifteen (15) days in 
duration or, at Buyer's option, an S-76 electrical training course approximately ten (10) days 
in duration. Either course includes inspection and maintenance troubleshooting and use of a 
maintenance trainer. Each mechanic must have background experience in one or more of 
the following categories: certified (by the FAA or by an equivalent airworthiness authority) 
airframe mechanic with one (1) year practical experience as a rated aircraft mechanic; one (1) 
year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military helicopter; or three (3) 
years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft mechanic. 
3. Engine Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer mechanics, an engine 
maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately five 
(5) days in duration.
