Assignment of Warranties and Training and Manufacturer's 
Consent 
This Assignment of Warranties and Training and Manufacturers Consent (this "Assignment') 
is made and entered into as of the date last executed, by and between Air Ghislane, Inc. (the 
"Assignor"), and Five Star Holding Company LLC (the 'Assignee"), and Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation 
(the "Manufacturer" or "Sikorsky'). 
WHEREAS, pursuant to the Sales Agreement No. S76TD6167 dated March 31, 2006, 
between Sikorsky and the Assignor (as amended, modified and supplemented from time to time) (the 
"Agreement"), the Assignor purchased a certain Sikorsky S76C++ helicopter bearing Manufacturers 
Serial No. 760867 (the `Aircraft"). A copy of the Agreement and all amendments exercised to date are 
attached hereto as Exhibit A. Under the Agreement, Assignor has, among others, certain rights with 
respect to remainder of training and warranty related to the Aircraft. Assignor now wishes to assign to 
Assignee, and Assignee wishes to accept the assignment of the remainder of the Assignor's Interest in 
the warranties and training under the Agreement (the "Warranties and Training"). 
WHEREAS, Sikorsky agrees to consent to•the Assignment (as defined herein).
NOW THEREFORE, in consideration for the mutual covenants and agreements herein, the 
receipt and sufficiency of which ere hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows: 
1. 
The Assignor hereby assigns to the Assignee all of Assignor's remaining rights and 
interest in the Warranties and Training. The Assignee hereby accepts such assignment, 
assumes all of the duties and obligations of the Assignor in respect of the Warranties and 
Training, and agrees to be bound by the terms of the Agreement in respect of the 
Warranties and Training in every way as if Assignee had been party to the Agreement as 
the "Customer" or the "Buyer" as at the date it was executed. 
2. 
For the avoidance of doubt, the Assignee agrees in exercising its rights under the 
Warranties and Training or in making any claim with respect to the Aircraft or other things 
delivered or to be delivered in connection therewith, it Is bound by and will comply with all 
applicable terms, conditions, and limitations of the Agreement. 
3. 
The Assignor authorizes the Assignee to exercise, to the exclusion of the Assignor, all 
rights and powers of the Assignor with respect to the Warranties and Training under the 
Agreement. With respect to the rights, powers, duties and obligations of the Assignor in 
respect of the Warranties and Training, all actions taken by the Assignee are final and 
binding on the Assignor. 
4. 
The Assignor confirms for the benefit of Sikorsky and the Assignee that it owns and 
controls the rights it purports to assign herein. 
5. 
The Assignor and the Assignee acknowledge and agree that Sikorsky's consent to the 
Assignment is only for the purpose of accommodating their separate business arrangement 
and that the parties do not Intend to expand Sikorsky's risk or liability obligations further 
than already present under the terms of the Agreement. Nothing contained herein shall 
subject Sikorsky to any liability to which it would not otherwise be subject under the 
Agreement or modify or waive in any respect the contract rights of Sikorsky thereunder, or 
constitute Sikorsky's consent to any further assignment or any obligations or rights therein 
by the parties hereto. 
6. 
The Assignee confirms for the benefit of Sikorsky that in exercising any rights of making 
any claims, including but not limited to those identified in this Assignment, the terms and 
conditions of the Agreement will apply and be binding on the Assignee, and Sikorsky shall 
have all the rights and defenses available to it in response to Assignee's exercise of such 
rights or making of such claims, to the same extent as if Assignee had been an original 
party thereto.

and not otherwise defined shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Agreement.

DEFINITIONS 
a) "AOG" means a Helicopter cannot fly in its current state solely as a result of a Component's 
failure; provided, however, that such failure or the absence of a replacement Component is not 
due to Customer's failure to comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. 
b) "Component" means those gear boxes identified as "covered" in Exhibit A. 
c) "CPU" means the most recent Sikorsky price list for certain parts used on the Helicopter, which 
is published by Sikorsky and typically updated at the beginning of each calendar year.

Hyperion Air, LLC S76D38751PAP 
d) "Dollars" or "M" means the lawful currency of the United States of America. 
e) "External Lift Cycle" means the Helicopter's performance of the following sequence of flight-
related activity: external load lift, enroute travel, approach to hover, and, release of load and 
land, or, release of load and depart. 
f) "Flight Time" means the time that commences when a helicopter moves under its own power 
for the purposes of flight and ends when the helicopter comes to rest after landing. A "Flight 
Hour" means sixty (60) minutes of Flight Time. 
g) "Owner" means the record title owner of the Helicopter(s). 
h) "Repetitive External Lift" means when the average number of External Lift Cycles exceeds 
six (6) per Flight Hour during any 250-Flight Hour period based on a moving average, 
calculated at intervals not to exceed fifty (50) Flight Hours of operation. 
i) "Time Between Overhaul" or "TBO" means the maximum number of Flight Hours that may 
be logged on a component before requiring removal for overhaul as specified in the then-
current Helicopter maintenance manual. 
II. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION 
1. Sikorsky's Obligation — 
a) When a Component covered by this Agreement requires overhaul or replacement 
(rendering it a "Non-Operational Component") during the term of this Agreement, 
Sikorsky shall, in its sole discretion, either (i) provide Customer with a new, overhauled or 
repaired Component of the same part number (a "Replacement Component"); or (ii) 
provide material and/or labor to repair the Non-Operational Component at the location of 
the Helicopter. A Replacement Component becomes a "Component" for purposes of this 
Agreement upon installation on the Helicopter for which it was provided. 
Only 
Components listed in Exhibit A or Replacement Components will be covered under this 
Agreement. Any other related or connected parts will not be covered by this Agreement; 
provided, however, that Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, elect to provide a part or labor 
service to prevent an unscheduled removal of a covered Component. 
b) For a Main Gear Box with Quiet Technology, strictly in the event of an AOG situation, 
Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, provide Customer with a Main Gear Box without the 
Quiet Technology in exchange for the Non-Operational Component to support the AOG. 
2. Ordering and Shipment of Replacement Components — To obtain a Replacement 
Component for a scheduled exchange requirement, Customer must issue a purchase order to 
Sikorsky a minimum of one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the requested delivery date. 
Purchase orders received by Sikorsky within less than one hundred twenty (120) days of the 
requested delivery date may be subject to additional delays. Each purchase order shall state 
shipping instructions and a requested delivery date. 
Sikorsky will ship Replacement

DEFINITIONS 
a) "AOG" means a Helicopter cannot fly in its current state solely as a result of a Component's 
failure; provided, however, that such failure or the absence of a replacement Component is not 
due to Customer's failure to comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. 
b) "Component" means those gear boxes identified as "covered" in Exhibit A. 
c) "CPL" means the most recent Sikorsky price list for certain pans used on the Helicopter, which 
is published by Sikorsky and typically updated at the beginning of each calendar year.

Hyperion Air, LLC S76D38751PAP 
d) "Dollars" or "M" means the lawful currency of the United States of America. 
e) "External Lift Cycle" means the Helicopter's performance of the following sequence of flight-
related activity: external load lift, enroute travel, approach to hover, and, release of load and 
land, or, release of load and depart. 
t) "Flight Time" means the time that commences when a helicopter moves under its own power 
for the purposes of flight and ends when the helicopter comes to rest after landing. A "Flight 
Hour" means sixty (60) minutes of Flight Time. 
g) "Owner" means the record title owner of the Helicopter(s). 
h) "Repetitive External Lift" means when the average number of External Lift Cycles exceeds 
six (6) per Flight Hour during any 250-Flight Hour period based on a moving average, 
calculated at intervals not to exceed fifty (50) Flight Hours of operation. 
i) "Time Between Overhaul" or "TBO" means the maximum number of Flight Hours that may 
be logged on a component before requiring removal for overhaul as specified in the then-
current Helicopter maintenance manual. 
II. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION 
1. Sikorsky's Obligation — 
a) When a Component covered by this Agreement requires overhaul or replacement 
(rendering it a "Non-Operational Component") during the term of this Agreement, 
Sikorsky shall, in its sole discretion, either (i) provide Customer with a new, overhauled or 
repaired Component of the same part number (a "Replacement Component"); or (ii) 
provide material and/or labor to repair the Non-Operational Component at the location of 
the Helicopter. A Replacement Component becomes a "Component" for purposes of this 
Agreement upon installation on the Helicopter for which it was provided. 
Only 
Components listed in Exhibit A or Replacement Components will be covered under this 
Agreement. Any other related or connected parts will not be covered by this Agreement; 
provided, however, that Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, elect to provide a part or labor 
service to prevent an unscheduled removal of a covered Component. 
b) For a Main Gear Box with Quiet Technology, strictly in the event of an AOG situation, 
Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, provide Customer with a Main Gear Box without the 
Quiet Technology in exchange for the Non-Operational Component to support the AOG. 
2. Ordering and Shipment of Replacement Components — To obtain a Replacement 
Component for a scheduled exchange requirement, Customer must issue a purchase order to 
Sikorsky a minimum of one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the requested delivery date. 
Purchase orders received by Sikorsky within less than one hundred twenty (120) days of the 
requested delivery date may be subject to additional delays. Each purchase order shall state 
shipping instructions and a requested delivery date.

reorganization or if a receiver, trustee, or custodian is appointed.

RAIN ASSURANCE PROGRAM AGREEMENT 
THIS POWERTRAIN ASSURANCE PROGRAM AGREEMENT (this "Agreement"),
dated as of the Acceptance Date set forth on the signature page hereto, is made by and between 
HELICOPTER SUPPORT, INC. D/B/A SIKORSKY COMMERCIAL, INC., a Connecticut 
corporation with a place of business at 124 Quarry Road, Trumbull, Connecticut 06611, United 
States ("Sikorsky") and HYPERION AIR LLC, a company with a place of business at 6100 Red 
Hook, Quarter B3, St. Thomas, United States Virgin Islands 00802 ("Customer"). Within this 
Agreement, Sikorsky and/or Customer shall each be a "Party" and collectively shall be the 
"Parties." 
WHEREAS, Sikorsky provides parts, service and support for owners and operators of Sikorsky 
Aircraft Corporation helicopters throughout the world, including an extended support plan for the 
gear boxes for the S-760 helicopter, known as the Powertrain Assurance Program ("PAP"); 
WHEREAS, on or about July 13, 2019 (the "Purchase Date"), Customer purchased from the 
owner the S-76 helicopter with serial number 760750; 
WHEREAS, Sikorsky was providing PAP for the gear boxes of such helicopter pursuant to the 
Powertrain Assurance Program Agreement (Contract No. 576112260PAP), dated as of July 1, 
2017, by and between Sikorsky and the helicopter's manager, Executive Jet Management, Inc. (the 
"Seller Contract"); 
WHEREAS, as a result of the sale, the manager has authorized, or intends to authorize, the transfer 
to Customer of all accruals under the Seller Contract as of the Sale Date in respect to such 
helicopter (the "Seller Authorization"). and 
WHEREAS, Customer desires to enter into this Agreement with Sikorsky to continue PAP 
coverage of such helicopter; 
NOW THEREFORE, for valid consideration mutually acknowledged by their signatures hereon, 
the Parties agree as follows:

DEFINITIONS 
a) "AOG" means a Helicopter cannot fly in its current state solely as a result of a Component's 
failure; provided, however, that such failure or the absence of a replacement Component is not 
due to Customer's failure to comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. 
b) "Component" means those gear boxes identified as "covered" in Exhibit A. 
c) "an," means the most recent Sikorsky price list for certain parts used on the Helicopter, 
which is published by Sikorsky and typically updated at the beginning of each calendar year. 
d) "Dollars" or "US$" means the lawful currency of the United States of America. 
e) "External Lift Cycle" means the Helicopter's performance of the following sequence of flight-
related activity: external load lift, enroute travel, approach to hover, and, release of load and 
land, or, release of load and depart. 
f) "Flight Time" means the time that commences when a helicopter moves under its own power 
for the purposes of flight and ends when the helicopter comes to rest after landing. A "Flight 
Hour" means sixty (60) minutes of Flight Time. 
g) "Owner" means the record title owner of the Helicopter(s). 
h) "Repetitive External Lift" means when the average number of External Lift Cycles exceeds 
six (6) per Flight Hour during any 250-Flight Hour period based on a moving average, 
calculated at intervals not to exceed fifty (50) Flight Hours of operation. 
i) "Time Between Overhaul" or "TBO" means the maximum number of Flight Hours that may 
be logged on a component before requiring removal for overhaul as specified in the then-
current Helicopter maintenance manual. 
II. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION 
1. Sikorsky's Obligation — 
a) When a Component covered by this Agreement requires overhaul or replacement 
(rendering it a "Non-Operational Component") during the term of this Agreement, 
Sikorsky shall, in its sole discretion, either (i) provide Customer with a new, overhauled or 
repaired Component of the same part number (a "Replacement Component"); or (ii) 
provide material and/or labor to repair the Non-Operational Component at the location of 
the Helicopter. A Replacement Component becomes a "Component" for purposes of this 
Agreement upon installation on the Helicopter for which it was provided. 
b) For a Main Gear Box with Quiet Technology, strictly in the event of an AOG situation, 
Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, provide Customer with a Main Gear Box without the 
Quiet Technology in exchange for the Non-Operational Component to support the AOG.

2. Ordering and Shipment of Replacement Components — To obtain a Replacement 
Component for a scheduled exchange requirement, Customer must issue a purchase order to 
Sikorsky a minimum of one hundred twenty (120) days prior to the requested delivery date. 
Purchase orders received by Sikorsky within less than one hundred twenty (120) days of the 
requested delivery date may be subject to additional delays. Each purchase order shall state 
shipping instructions and a requested delivery date. 
Sikorsky will ship Replacement 
Components to Customer at Customer's expense, FCA Sikorsky's designated facility 
(Incoterms 2010). Sikorsky and Customer expressly agree that any additional terms and 
conditions set forth in Customer's purchase order shall have no effect and that the terms and 
conditions of this Agreement shall govern all purchase orders issued by Customer to Sikorsky 
hereunder. 
In the case of an unscheduled exchange requirement, Sikorsky shall use 
commercially reasonable efforts to deliver the Replacement Component as soon as possible. 
3. Exchange/Return of Non-Operational Component - Customer shall, at its own expense, 
return the Non-Operational Component to Sikorsky within thirty (30) days of Sikorsky's 
shipment of the Replacement Component and shall provide documentation to Sikorsky to 
confirm return shipment details. If Customer fails to provide documentation that the shipment 
of a Non-Operational Component has been initiated within such time period, Customer shall 
pay to Sikorsky a late return fee of one hundred sixty dollars ($160.00USD) per Component, 
per day in excess of the thirty (30) day return period. If Sikorsky has not received a Non-
Operational Component within six (6) months from the date of Sikorsky's shipment of the 
Replacement Component, then Customer shall pay to Sikorsky the price for the Replacement 
Component as listed in Sikorsky's CPL (the "Non-Return Fee"). Should Sikorsky subsequently 
receive the Non-Operational Component, Sikorsky shall credit to Customer's account an 
amount equal to ninety percent (90%) of the Non-Return Fee. The Non-Operational 
Component should be packed in the same container(s) (or Sikorsky-approved equivalent) in 
which the Replacement Component was received. Customer shall be responsible for any 
additional repair costs due to damage associated with an improperly packaged Non-
Operational Component and/or any damage caused by Customer at the time of removal of the 
Non-Operational Component. Customer shall provide Sikorsky with a copy of the Non-
Operational Component log card prior to shipment, and shall include the original log card in 
the return container with the Non-Operational Component. Customer shall also retain a copy 
of the Non-Operational Component log card. 
4. Title Transfer/Risk of Loss - Title and risk of loss for each Replacement Component supplied 
to Customer under this Agreement shall be deemed to have been transferred to Customer upon 
shipment from Sikorsky's facility. Title and risk of loss for each Non-Operational Component 
shall be deemed to have been transferred to Sikorsky upon delivery to Sikorsky's facility. 
Customer represents and warrants that, at the time title to any Non-Operational Component is 
transferred to Sikorsky (thereby constituting a sale), Customer will have full power, authority 
and legal right to sell such Non-Operational Component to Sikorsky, and such Non-
Operational Component will be free and clear of any liens, charges and encumbrances created 
by or against Customer or arising out of the ownership, possession, operation or use of such 
Non-Operational Component. Customer hereby indemnifies and holds Sikorsky harmless 
from any breach of the foregoing representation and warranty.

5. Transportation and Labor Costs for Failures within One Hundred Hours — If a 
Replacement Component from Sikorsky fails upon installation or within one hundred (100) 
hours of installation, Sikorsky's sole and exclusive obligation shall be to reimburse Customer: 
(i) the actual and documented transportation costs for the return of the Non-Operational 
Component to Sikorsky and shipment of the Replacement Component to Customer; (ii) up to, 
but not exceeding, four thousand dollars ($4,000.00USD) for labor costs associated with 
removal of a Main Gear Box; and (iii) up to, but not exceeding, seven hundred fifty dollars 
($750.00USD) for labor costs associated with removal of other Components covered by this 
Agreement. Customer shall be responsible for all other transportation and labor costs in excess 
of the amounts noted herein. 
III. CUSTOMER'S OBLIGATIONS 
1. Administration of Agreement by Customer — If Customer is not also the Owner of a 
Helicopter, without releasing Customer from any contractual obligations hereunder, Customer 
represents and warrants that it is authorized by the Owner to operate and maintain the 
Helicopter, to administer this Agreement and to be the primary point of contact for billing, 
technical support, logistics support, reporting, and other administrative matters pertaining to 
the Helicopter and arising under this Agreement. Customer shall save, indemnify, defend and 
hold harmless Sikorsky and its corporate parents and subsidiaries from and against all claims, 
losses, damages, costs (including legal costs), expenses and liabilities arising from or relating 
to disputes between Customer and Owner pertaining to this Agreement. Upon request, 
Customer shall provide to Sikorsky the Owner's written acknowledgment of the foregoing in 
a form reasonably acceptable to Sikorsky. 
2. Flight Time Reporting - Within fifteen (15) days after the end of each month, Customer shall 
e-mail to Sikorsky a statement, signed by Customer, reporting the Component serial numbers 
installed on each Helicopter, the time since new and time since overhaul (if the Component 
was previously overhauled) for each Component, and the total Flight Hours (reporting should 
be to the nearest tenth of an hour) for each Helicopter during the prior month (the "Flight Time 
Report") to fleet_program_finance.gr-sik®Imco.com. 
Alternatively, Customer may use 
Sikorsky's customer portal at www.sikorsky360.com to report monthly Flight Hours via the 
Online Flight Time Report. 
Customer warrants to Sikorsky that all data reported will be correct, and further agrees to grant 
Sikorsky or its designated representative access to Helicopter records upon reasonable request. 
If the Flight Time Report is not received within fifteen ( l5) days after the end of each month, 
Sikorsky shall notify Customer of such delinquency. If the Flight Time Report is not received 
within thirty (30) days after providing of such notification, Sikorsky may terminate this 
Agreement or remove the Helicopter from coverage hereunder in accordance with the 
termination provisions of Article V. 
Electronic Flight Time Reports will be updated annually and can be provided to Customer 
upon request, reflecting the Flight Hour Fee for the current calendar year.

IV. PAYMENT AND ADDITIONAL CHARGES 
1. Entry Payment — 
(a) With respect to each Component, upon execution of this Agreement, Customer agrees to 
pay to Sikorsky an entry payment for each such Component equal to the applicable Flight 
Hour Fee set forth in Article I multiplied by the number of Flight Hours accrued on such 
Component between the Sale Date and the Acceptance Date of this Agreement (if any). 
(b) With respect to any Component added to coverage after the Acceptance Date of this 
Agreement, upon of the, upon execution of an amendment adding such Component to 
coverage hereunder, Customer agrees to pay to Sikorsky an entry payment for each such 
Component equal to the applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article I multiplied by the 
number of Flight Hours accrued on such Component since the Component was new or 
overhauled (as the case may be) at the time of entry into coverage hereunder. 
2. Flight Hour Fee — Customer shall pay monthly for each Component an amount equal to the 
applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article I multiplied by the actual Flight Hours of 
operation for the applicable Helicopter, as set forth in the Flight Time Report. Customer shall 
calculate the total Flight Hour Fee for each month (even when zero (0) hours are flown) via 
the Flight Time Report no later than fifteen (15) days following the end of the month. Sikorsky 
shall generate an invoice for the total monthly Flight Hour Fee. Customer may also use the 
Flight Time Report as a self-generated invoice document. 
After the end of each calendar year and upon termination, expiration or transfer of this 
Agreement, Sikorsky shall invoice Customer for each Component an amount equal to (i) the 
difference, if any, between the Minimum Utilization Flight Hours set forth in Article I and the 
actual Flight Hours flown, multiplied by (ii) the applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article 
I. 
3. Unused Hour Charge — Except in the case of an unscheduled exchange requirement removed 
pursuant to Article 111.6 above, if Customer removes a Component prior to the approved TBO 
for such Component with at least one hundred (100) Flight Hours remaining (the difference 
between the TBO and the hours at removal referred to as the "Unused Hours"), Customer shall 
pay to Sikorsky an amount equal to: (A) the applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article I, 
multiplied by (B) the difference between the number of Unused Hours less one hundred (100). 
4. Upgradeable Component Charge — Upon election of a Component upgrade in the future, 
Sikorsky shall invoice and Customer shall pay the mutually agreed price for such upgrade. 
5. Overhaul Charge — For any Components not covered by a preceding PAP agreement, 
Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, charge Customer additional amounts related to repair work

operating conditions.

covered under this Agreement without Sikorsky's prior written approval.

without Sikorsky's written approval, as set forth in Article V.3 below.

for a period of thirty (30) days after notice by Sikorsky.

DEFINITIONS 
a) "AOG" means a Helicopter cannot fly in its current state solely as a result of a Component's 
failure; provided, however, that such failure or the absence of a replacement Component is not 
due to Customer's failure to comply with the terms and conditions of this Agreement. 
b) "Component" means those gear boxes identified as "covered" in Exhibit A. 
c) "an," means the most recent Sikorsky price list for certain pans used on the Helicopter, 
which is published by Sikorsky and typically updated at the beginning of each calendar year. 
d) "Dollars" or "US$" means the lawful currency of the United States of America. 
e) "External Lift Cycle" means the Helicopter's performance of the following sequence of flight-
related activity: external load lift, enroute travel, approach to hover, and, release of load and 
land, or, release of load and depart. 
f) "Flight Time" means the time that commences when a helicopter moves under its own power 
for the purposes of flight and ends when the helicopter comes to rest after landing. A "Flight 
Hour" means sixty (60) minutes of Flight Time. 
g) "Owner" means the record title owner of the Helicopter(s). 
h) "Repetitive External Lift" means when the average number of External Lift Cycles exceeds 
six (6) per Flight Hour during any 250-Flight Hour period based on a moving average, 
calculated at intervals not to exceed fifty (50) Flight Hours of operation. 
i) "Time Between Overhaul" or "TBO" means the maximum number of Flight Hours that may 
be logged on a component before requiring removal for overhaul as specified in the then-
current Helicopter maintenance manual. 
II. PROGRAM DESCRIPTION 
1. Sikorsky's Obligation — 
a) When a Component covered by this Agreement requires overhaul or replacement 
(rendering it a "Non-Operational Component") during the term of this Agreement, 
Sikorsky shall, in its sole discretion, either (i) provide Customer with a new, overhauled or 
repaired Component of the same part number (a "Replacement Component"); or (ii) 
provide material and/or labor to repair the Non-Operational Component at the location of 
the Helicopter. A Replacement Component becomes a "Component" for purposes of this 
Agreement upon installation on the Helicopter for which it was provided. 
b) For a Main Gear Box with Quiet Technology, strictly in the event of an AOG situation, 
Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, provide Customer with a Main Gear Box without the 
Quiet Technology in exchange for the Non-Operational Component to support the AOG.

which the Replacement Component was received. Customer shall be responsible for any 
additional repair costs due to damage associated with an improperly packaged Non-
Operational Component and/or any damage caused by Customer at the time of removal of the

Operational Component log card prior to shipment, and shall include the original log card in 
the return container with the Non-Operational Component. Customer shall also retain a copy 
of the Non-Operational Component log card.

IV. PAYMENT AND ADDITIONAL CHARGES 
1. Entry Payment — 
(a) With respect to each Component, upon execution of this Agreement, Customer agrees to 
pay to Sikorsky an entry payment for each such Component equal to the applicable Flight 
Hour Fee set forth in Article I multiplied by the number of Flight Hours accrued on such 
Component between the Sale Date and the Acceptance Date of this Agreement (if any). 
(b) With respect to any Component added to coverage after the Acceptance Date of this 
Agreement, upon of the, upon execution of an amendment adding such Component to 
coverage hereunder, Customer agrees to pay to Sikorsky an entry payment for each such 
Component equal to the applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article I multiplied by the 
number of Flight Hours accrued on such Component since the Component was new or 
overhauled (as the case may be) at the time of entry into coverage hereunder. 
2. Flight Hour Fee — Customer shall pay monthly for each Component an amount equal to the 
applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article I multiplied by the actual Flight Hours of 
operation for the applicable Helicopter, as set forth in the Flight Time Report. Customer shall 
calculate the total Flight Hour Fee for each month (even when zero (0) hours are flown) via 
the Flight Time Report no later than fifteen (15) days following the end of the month. Sikorsky 
shall generate an invoice for the total monthly Flight Hour Fee. Customer may also use the 
Flight Time Report as a self-generated invoice document. 
After the end of each calendar year and upon termination, expiration or transfer of this 
Agreement, Sikorsky shall invoice Customer for each Component an amount equal to (i) the 
difference, if any, between the Minimum Utilization Flight Hours set forth in Article I and the 
actual Flight Hours flown, multiplied by (ii) the applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article 
I. 
3. Unused Hour Charge — Except in the case of an unscheduled exchange requirement removed 
pursuant to Article 111.6 above, if Customer removes a Component prior to the approved TBO 
for such Component with at least one hundred (100) Flight Hours remaining (the difference 
between the TBO and the hours at removal referred to as the "Unused Hours"), Customer shall 
pay to Sikorsky an amount equal to: (A) the applicable Flight Hour Fee set forth in Article I, 
multiplied by (B) the difference between the number of Unused Hours less one hundred (100). 
4. Upgradeable Component Charge — Upon election of a Component upgrade in the future, 
Sikorsky shall invoice and Customer shall pay the mutually agreed price for such upgrade. 
5. Overhaul Charge — For any Components not covered by a preceding PAP agreement, 
Sikorsky may, in its sole discretion, charge Customer additional amounts related to repair work

Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe Executive Helicopter"). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary

2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for 
acceptance at the Sikorsky designated facility in Connecticut (the "Designated Facility") on 
the Scheduled Presentation Dates. Upon Buyer's request for a demonstration flight of the 
Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight at the Designated Facility during 
such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or longer as 
may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is conditioned 
upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy condition with all 
flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has been manufactured in 
accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the Helicopter has no damage, 
corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Title Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall evidence 
its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance. Upon 
Buyers execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and payment of the Baseline 
Helicopter Final Payment pursuant to Section III.1.b., Sikorsky shall transfer title to Buyer at 
the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky shall provide to Buyer a FAA 
Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty Bill of Sale (Exhibit C). Sikorsky 
shall retain custody of the Helicopter for the purpose of the performance of the Completion 
Services. As part of the Completion Services, Sikorsky will transport the Helicopter, at 
Sikorsky's expense, from Connecticut, to Sikorsky's designated completion center (the 
"Completion Center") via ferry flight. Upon its arrival at the Completion Center, the Helicopter 
shall be inducted into the facility in order to allow the performance of the Completion 
Services. 
4. No Prospective Registration of Interest- Prior to the transfer of title as provided in this 
Agreement, Buyer, without the prior written consent of Sikorsky, shall neither register nor 
consent to the ability of any person to register any interest in the Helicopter or its engines on 
the International Registry, including without limitation, any prospective international interest, 
pursuant to that body of law know as the Cape Town Treaty Convention on International 
Interests in Mobile Equipment and the Protocol to the Convention on International Interests in 
Mobile Equipment on Matters Specific to Aircraft Equipment (hereinafter the "Cape Town 
Treaty"). Any consent by Sikorsky to registration of any interest in the Helicopter or its 
engines shall be subject to among other things at Sikorsky's sole discretion, receipt by 
Sikorsky of all payments due under this Agreement at the time of title transfer of the 
Helicopter to Buyer. Registration of any interest under the Cape Town Treaty in violation of 
this paragraph shall be deemed ineffective as against Sikorsky and Buyer shall immediately 
upon request of Sikorsky and at Buyers expense, take all required action to remove any such 
interest or other encumbrance on the Helicopter in connection therewith. 
5. Risk of Loss - Sikorsky shall have risk of loss of the Helicopter, subsequent to the transfer of 
title through Buyer's acceptance of the Completion Services. In the event that the Helicopter 
is damaged or the functionality is in any way compromised during the conduct of the 
Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the Completion Services, to 
repair such damage or restore such functionality to as good condition as new. Buyer agrees 
that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid directly to Sikorsky. In the event

VI - HELICOPTER RELATED PROVISIONS 
1. 
Type Design and Production Approval - The S-76 helicopter and all of its variants has 
been granted Type Certification by the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration ("FAA") under 
Federal Aviation Regulation ("FAR") Title 14 CFR Part 21. The certification basis of the S-76 
as defined by Type Certificate H1 NE, is FAR Title 14 CFR Part 29, "Airworthiness Standards: 
Transport Category Rotorcraft". Manufacture of the S-76C++ helicopter is approved under 
Sikorsky's Production Certificate PC-105 granted in accordance with FAR Title 14 CFR Part 
21. Sikorsky as Type Certificate Holder, in the course and conduct of its business may at its 
sole discretion, seek FAA approval for the manufacture of the Helicopter under Sikorsky's 
Type Certificate at any facility wholly owned and controlled by Sikorsky and approved for such 
manufacture by FAA.

VII - TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Initial Pilot Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 initial pilot training 
course approximately ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual Flight Rules ("VFR") 
transition segment and, as required, an Instrument Flight Rules ("IFR") transition segment. 
Each of the segments is programmed to provide emphasis on helicopter familiarization, 
classroom instruction on systems operation and instruction in both the S-76 Simulator and the 
S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In addition, each Buyer pilot will receive two and one half (2.5) hours of 
flight with an instructor pilot. 
Each Buyer pilot must have a current U.S. commercial 
helicopter certificate or equivalent, and for the IFR segment, each Buyer pilot must have a 
current commercial certificate helicopter instrument rating, or equivalent. All flight training 
shall be conducted on the Deluxe Executive Helicopter to be delivered hereunder, following 
acceptance by the Buyer and transfer of title to the Buyer. 
2. Initial Maintenance or Electrical Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer 
mechanics an initial S-76 maintenance training course approximately fifteen (15) days in 
duration or, at Buyer's option, an S-76 electrical training course approximately ten (10) days 
in duration. Either course includes inspection and maintenance troubleshooting and use of a 
maintenance trainer. Each mechanic must have background experience in one or more of 
the following categories: certified (by the FAA or by an equivalent airworthiness authority) 
airframe mechanic with one (1) year practical experience as a rated aircraft mechanic; one (1) 
year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military helicopter; or three (3) 
years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft mechanic. 
3. Engine Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer mechanics, an engine 
maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately five 
(5) days in duration.

HELICOPTER CONFIGURATION 
EXHIBIT A 
The following items of standard and optional equipment as described below, which have been 
selected by the Buyer, shall be installed on the Helicopter to be delivered under the Agreement. 
Part 1: 
BASELINE AIRCRAFT 
Features of the S-76C++ Aircraft Code 0102: 
Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated main rotor system with 
dual controls. 
Cockpit — An Integrated Instrument Display System (IIDS), with an easy to upgrade avionics package. There 
is a Bleed Air Heating Defogging system and dual windshield wipers. The Pilot and Copilot seats come with a 
five point Restraint system. 
Cabin — A large cabin that can be configured for four different missions and a 38 cubic foot baggage 
compartment 
Other — Retractable landing gear, and 281 gallons of usable fuel 
Baseline Avionics Package Includes: 
Collins Proline II: Dual Collins VHF 22A Comms and VIR 32 Nays, single ADF 462 ADF, TDR 90 
Transponder, DME 42 DME with IND 42A Indicator, ALT 1000 Radio Altimeter with Expanded Scale ALI 55A 
Indicator. 
Honeywell EFIS/DAFCS: 4-Tube Honeywell EDZ 756 EFIS with 5" x 6" Indicators Displaying Airspeed, 
Altitude and Vertical Speed, Dual Litef AHRS, Dual Penny and Giles Air Data Computers, Dual Honeywell 
Digital SPZ 7600 Automatic Flight Control System, Altitude Alert. 
Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC Generator, Dual 
Static Inverters, Avionics and EFIS Master Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance jacks, one in the 
cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 45O pedestal mounted ICS foot switches, 
three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-around cord and two 30-foot walk-around cords, Cabin 
PA/Chime System, and a Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 CVR, 3" Backup 
Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-335D Standby Attitude Indicator with Nav1/Nav2 Select, ELT 406-NHM 
w/ Satellite Frequency, Electric Door Locks — Cabin, Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440. Windshield Washer System, Heated Glass 
Windshields. and Engine Inlet Barrier Filter

AIRCRAFT PAINT - STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE 
• 
Wash and degrease aircraft. 
• 
Remove Cowlings/antennas and reinstall after painting. 
• Remove main rotor blades and store. 
• 
Remove Chaff Tape and replace during detailing, if required. 
• 
Wrap windows, landing gear, access panels, engine and transmission. 
• 
Sand aircraft. 
• 
Repair any damage (after customer's approval)/ apply fill primer. 
• 
Remove doors. 
• 
Wrap door frames 
• 
Apply self-etching primer to airframe as required. 
• 
Apply fill primer to composite areas as required. 
• Mix paint to customer's selection. 
• 
Apply three coats of base paint to aircraft and two coats of clear. 
• 
Apply three coats of stripes and two coats of clear. 
• 
Apply registration "N" number and decals. 
• 
Cowlings and doors are installed onto aircraft for layout and removed for painting 
separately from airframe. 
• 
Hardware will be left unpainted. 
• 
Detail aircraft after removal from paint booth.

1. Sale - Sikorsky shall sell and deliver to the Buyer, and the Buyer shall purchase from 
Sikorsky, the Quantity of one new Sikorsky Model S-76C Helicopters with new 
Turbomeca 2S2 engines (known as the S-76C++) and equipped with the items of 
additional equipment specified in Exhibit A, Part 1 (the "Helicopter"). 
In addition, 
Sikorsky shall sell and perform the Completion Services for Buyer and Buyer shall 
purchase the Completion Services on the Helicopter, which will then be equipped with 
the items of additional equipment specified in Exhibit A, Part 2, (the Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter"). 
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, during the 
performance of the Completion Services, the configuration items specified in Annex 1 to 
Exhibit A shall be removed from the Helicopter and retained as property of Sikorsky. 
These configuration items shall be either deleted or replaced by the customized options 
chosen by Buyer in Exhibit A, Part 2 as part of the Completion Services. 
2. Presentation of Helicopter for Acceptance - The Helicopter shall be presented for 
acceptance at the Sikorsky designated facility in Connecticut (the "Designated Facility") 
on the Scheduled Presentation Dates. Upon Buyer's request for a demonstration flight of 
the Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a demonstration flight at the Designated Facility 
during such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or 
longer as may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is 
conditioned upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy 
condition with all flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has 
been manufactured in accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the 
Helicopter has no damage, corrosion or other defects. 
3. Acceptance and Title Transfer - After presentation of the Helicopter, Buyer shall 
evidence its acceptance of the Helicopter by executing a Certificate of Helicopter 
Acceptance. Upon Buyer's execution of the Certificate of Helicopter Acceptance, and

4. Risk of Loss — Sikorsky shall have risk of loss of the Helicopter, subsequent to the 
transfer of title through Buyer's acceptance of the Completion Services. In the event that 
the Helicopter is damaged or the functionality is in any way compromised during the 
conduct of the Completion Services, Sikorsky shall be required, as a part of the 
Completion Services, to repair such damage or restore such functionality to as good 
condition as new. Buyer agrees that any insurance proceeds for such repair shall be paid 
directly to Sikorsky. In the event the Helicopter is lost or destroyed or damaged beyond 
economic repair at any time prior to Buyer's acceptance, Buyer shall have the right to 
either (i) purchase the next available S-76 C++ Helicopter in Sikorsky's production 
sequence (the "Replacement Helicopter") on the same terms and conditions as set forth in 
this Agreement, (however Sikorsky reserves the right to make changes in the Exhibit A 
configuration and Helicopter Unit Price of the Replacement Helicopter required due to 
obsolescence, FAA requirements, or as a result of changes in the manufacture of the 
Helicopter), or (ii) terminate this Agreement. Buyer shall notify Sikorsky of its decision 
within fifteen (15) days of receipt by Buyer of written notice from Sikorsky of the loss or 
destruction of or damage beyond economic repair to the Helicopter, which notice shall 
include the projected delivery date of the Replacement Helicopter. 
5. Presentation of Completion Services for Acceptance — Upon the completion of the 
Completion Services, the Deluxe Executive Helicopter shall be presented for technical 
acceptance of the work performed at the Completion Center on the Scheduled 
Presentation Date Completion Services. Upon Buyer's request for an inspection and 
demonstration flight of the Deluxe Executive Helicopter, Sikorsky shall conduct a 
demonstration flight of the Deluxe Executive Helicopter, at the Completion Center during 
such inspection and presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in 
duration or longer as may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to accept the 
Deluxe Executive Helicopter is conditioned upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that 
the Completion Services have been satisfactorily completed and that the Helicopter as 
previously accepted by Buyer, is in airworthy condition with all systems functional and in 
proper working order and with no damage incurred. 
6. Acceptance of Completion Services - After the completion of the inspection, the Deluxe

Services at the Designated Facility. Buyer shall evidence its acceptance of the Completion 
Services by executing a Certificate of Acceptance of the Completion Services (Exhibit

TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Initial Pilot Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and 
delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 
initial pilot training course approximately ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual 
Flight Rules ("VFR") transition segment and, as required, an Instrument Flight Rules 
("IFR") transition segment. Each of the segments is programmed to provide emphasis on 
helicopter familiarization, classroom instruction on systems operation and instruction in 
both the S-76 Simulator and the S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In addition, each Buyer pilot will 
receive two and one half (2.5) hours of flight with an instructor pilot. Each Buyer pilot 
must have a current U.S. commercial helicopter certificate or equivalent, and for the IFR 
segment, each Buyer pilot must have a current commercial certificate helicopter

mechanic; one (1) year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military 
helicopter; or three (3) years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft 
mechanic.

HELICOPTER CONFIGURATION 
The following items of standard and optional equipment as described below, which have been 
selected by the Buyer, shall be installed on the Helicopter to he delivered under the Agreement. 
Part 1: 
BASELINE AIRCRAFT 
Features of the S-76C++ Aircraft Code 0102: 
Dynamic System - Two Turbomeca Arriel 2S2 engines, and a four blade articulated 
main rotor system with dual controls. 
Cockpit  — An Integrated Instrument Display System (IIDS), with an easy to upgrade 
avionics package. There is a Bleed Air Heating Defogging system and dual windshield 
wipers. The Pilot and Copilot seats come with a five point Restraint system. 
Cabin  — A large cabin that can be configured for four different missions and a 38 cubic 
foot baggage compartment 
Other  — Retractable landing gear, and 281 gallons of usable fuel 
Baseline Avionics Package Includes: 
Collins Proline II: Dual Collins VHF 22A Comms and VIR 32 Nays, single ADF 462 ADF, 
TDR 90 Transponder, DME 42 DME with IND 42A Indicator, ALT 55B Radio Altimeter 
with Expanded Scale ALI 55A Indicator. 
Honeywell EFIS/DAFCS: 4-Tube Honeywell EDZ 756 EFIS with 5" x 6" Indicators 
Displaying Airspeed, Altitude and Vertical Speed, Dual Litef AHRS, Dual Penny and 
Giles Air Data Computers, Dual Honeywell Digital SPZ 7600 Automatic Flight Control 
System, Altitude Alert. 
Electrical: 28 Volt Electrical System with two 200 Amp Starter/Generators, 10 KVA AC 
Generator, Dual Static Inverters, Avionics and EFIS Master Switches. 
Audio: Dual dB Systems Audio control panels with ICS and VOX plus three maintenance 
jacks, one in the cabin and two in the baggage compartment. This also includes dual 
45° pedestal mounted ICS foot switches, three David Clark Headsets, one six-foot walk-
around cord and two 30-foot walk-around cords, Cabin PA/Chime System, and a 
Passenger Briefing System - PBS 250 
Backup/Safety Systems: Enhanced Ground Proximity Warning System, Universal 120 
CVR, 3" Backup Airspeed Indicator and Altimeter, ADI-335D Standby Attitude Indicator 
with Nav1/Nav2 Select, ELT 406-NHM w/ Satellite Frequency, Electric Door Locks —
Cabin, Cabin/Cockpit and FD DCPL Chime/Annunciator 
Weather Related Systems: Wx Avoidance Radar - Primus 440, Windshield Washer 
System, Heated Glass Windshields, and Engine Inlet Barrier Filter

A. REPAIR/REPLACEMENT 
Sikorsky shall be obligated under this warranty to the repair or replacement of the 
defective item with a new, overhauled or serviceable replacement item during the 
applicable term of the warranty. The decision to repair or replace the defective item is 
solely at the discretion of Sikorsky exercised with reasonable care. 
Replacement parts that are life limited shall have hourly, calendar or cycle lives 
remaining equal or greater than the hourly, calendar or cycle lives remaining of the 
parts being replaced (whichever is applicable, and if more than one is applicable, 
whichever is greater), unless otherwise agreed by the parties. If Helicopter Support, 
Inc (HSI) does not have a part whose life is equal to or less than the one removed, 
HSI shall contact Buyer and it would be the Buyer's option whether to accept an 
exchange or to arrange for a loaner while Buyer's is being repaired.

automatically become the property of Sikorsky.

pertinent Deluxe Executive Helicopter operational and maintenance records.

period immediately preceding the discovery as well as records of any incident, 
accident, or unusual event encountered by the Deluxe Executive Helicopter at 
any time prior to the discovery of the defect.

defective goods to Sikorsky, their reshipment to Buyer, and the risk of loss thereof, up 
to and including the average cost of Federal Express P1 or equivalent, will be borne 
by Sikorsky if returned in accordance with written shipping instructions from 
Sikorsky. Transportation charges do not include taxes, duties, loans, lease charges, 
exchange fees, warehousing charges, handling charges, or administrative charges 
when charged by a party other than Sikorsky or a Sikorsky subcontractor. Any 
premium transportation costs shall be borne by the Buyer.

during such presentation, which flight shall be approximately one (1) hour in duration or 
longer as may reasonably be necessary. Buyer's obligation to purchase the Helicopter is 
conditioned upon and subject to Buyer being satisfied that the Helicopter is in airworthy 
condition with all flight critical systems functional and in proper working order, and has 
been manufactured in accordance with the specifications of this Agreement and that the 
Helicopter has no damage, corrosion or other defects.

shall transfer title to Buyer at the Designated Facility. Following title transfer, Sikorsky 
shall provide to Buyer a FAA Certificate of Airworthiness, a Bill of Sale and a Warranty

VIII. 
TRAINING PROVISIONS 
1. Initial Pilot Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and 
delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer pilots an S-76 
initial pilot training course approximately ten (10) days in duration, consisting of a Visual 
Flight Rules ("VFR") transition segment and, as required, an Instrument Flight Rules 
("1FR') transition segment. Each of the segments is programmed to provide emphasis on 
helicopter familiarization, classroom instruction on systems operation and instruction in 
both the S-76 Simulator and the S-76 Cockpit Trainer. In addition, each Buyer pilot will 
receive two and one half (2.5) hours of flight with an instructor pilot. Each Buyer pilot 
must have a current U.S. commercial helicopter certificate or equivalent, and for the IFR 
segment, each Buyer pilot must have a current commercial certificate helicopter 
instrument rating, or equivalent All flight training shall be conducted on the Deluxe 
Executive Helicopter to be delivered hereunder, following acceptance by the Buyer and 
transfer of title to the Buyer. 
2. Initial Maintenance or Electrical Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive 
Helicopter sold and delivered hereunder, Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer 
mechanics an initial S-76 maintenance training course approximately fifteen (15) days in 
duration or, at Buyer's option, an S-76 electrical training course approximately ten (10) 
days in duration_ Either course includes inspection and maintenance troubleshooting and 
use of a maintenance trainer. Each mechanic must have background experience in one or 
more of the following categories: certified (by the FAA, or by an equivalent airworthiness 
authority) airframe mechanic with one (I) year practical experience as a rated aircraft 
mechanic; one (1) year experience as an active mechanic on a commercial or military 
helicopter; or three (3) years general experience as a commercial or military aircraft 
mechanic. 
3. Engine Training Services - With each Deluxe Executive Helicopter sold and delivered 
hereunder., Sikorsky shall make available to three (3) Buyer mechanics, an engine 
maintenance course at the engine manufacturer's facility. This course is approximately 
five (5) days in duration. 
4. Scheduling - Within thirty days of Buyer's execution of the Agreement, the Buyer shall 
provide Sikorsky written notice as to whether the Buyer's personnel or designees are 
going to attend the S-76 pilot training and/or maintenance/electrical training courses.

use and service for the periods outlined below. Normal Use and Service shall mean the 
operation and maintenance of the Helicopter, sub-assemblies, and parts in accordance

3. SIKORSKY OBLIGATIONS 
A. REPAIR/REPLACEMENT 
Sikorsky shall be obligated under this warranty to the repair or replacement of the 
defective item with a new, overhauled or serviceable replacement item during the 
applicable term of the warranty. The decision to repair or replace the defective item is 
solely at the discretion of Sikorsky exercised with reasonable care. 
Replacement parts that are life limited shall have hourly, calendar or cycle lives 
remaining equal or greater than the hourly, calendar or cycle lives remaining of the 
parts being replaced (whichever is applicable, and if more than one is applicable, 
whichever is greater), unless otherwise agreed by the parties. If Helicopter Support, 
Inc (HST) does not have a part whose life is equal to or less than the one removed, 
HSI shall contact Buyer and it would be the Buyer's option whether to accept an 
exchange or to arrange for a loaner while Buyer's is being repaired.

A. 
The Buyer must notify Sikorsky in writing of any defect occurring within the

If Sikorsky elects to replace or exchange rather than repair and return the 
warranted item the Buyer must return the defective part reasonably requested to 
Sikorsky or its designated repair facility within 30 days (domestic) or 60 days 
(international) of receipt of a replacement/ exchange item, if so requested by 
Sikorsky. Any defective item that is replaced or exchanged by Sikorsky shall 
automatically become the property of Sikorsky. 
C. 
If requested by Sikorsky, the Buyer must furnish Sikorsky with copies of 
pertinent Deluxe Executive Helicopter operational and maintenance records. 
Such records may include any and all those prepared during the entire warranty 
period immediately preceding the discovery as well as records of any incident, 
accident, or unusual event encountered by the Deluxe Executive Helicopter at 
any time prior to the discovery of the defect. 
5. TRANSPORTATION 
Transportation charges relating to approved warranty claims for the return of 
defective goods to Sikorsky, their reshipment to Buyer, and the risk of loss thereof, up 
to and including the average cost of Federal Express P1 or equivalent, will be borne 
by Sikorsky if returned in accordance with written shipping instructions from 
Sikorsky. Transportation charges do not include taxes, duties, loans, lease charges, 
exchange fees, warehousing charges, handling charges, or administrative charges 
when charged by a party other than Sikorsky or a Sikorsky subcontractor. Any 
premium transportation costs shall be borne by the Buyer.

TERMINATION AGREEMENT 
THIS TERMINATION AGREEMENT ("Termination Agreement") is made this 
tk day of March 2011 ("Effective Date") between Sikorsky International Operations, 
Inc., ("Sikorsky"), and Freedom Air International, Inc. f/k/a Air Ghislaine, Inc. (TAI") 
(together the 'Parties"). 
WHEREAS, on or about October 20, 2006, Sikorsky and Air Ghislaine, Inc. (n/k/a 
Freedom Air International, Inc.) executed S-76D Position 
Agreement 
No. 
S76DDA050082 ('Position Agreement"), whereby Sikorsky agreed to assign to Air 
Ghislaine, Inc. the Estimated Baseline Helicopter Delivery Date and Estimated 
Completion Services Date as outlined in the Position Agreement, to one (1) Sikorsky 
Model S-76D Helicopter ("Helicopter"); 
WHEREAS, on February 11. 2010 and July 6, 2010, Certificates of Amendment 
to the original Certificate of Incorporation of FAI were filed with the Delaware Secretary 
of State on February 11, 2010 and July 6, 2010, changing its corporate name first from 
Air Ghislaine, Inc. to Shimitka Air, Inc., and then from Shmitka Air, Inc. to Freedom Air 
International, Inc., respectively; and 
WHEREAS, the Parties are now mutually agreeing to terminate the Position 
Agreement. 
NOW. THEREFORE, in consideration of the premises and for other good and 
valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which is hereby acknowledged, the 
Parties hereby agree as follows: 
1. 
As of the Effective Date, the Position Agreement is terminated. 
2. 
The Parties hereby release and forever discharge one another of and from 
all actions, causes of action, suits, debts, obligations, claims and demands

WEB HELOTRAC LICENSE AGREEMENT 
This WEB RELOTRAC License Agreement (hereinafter the "Agreement") is by and between 
Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation, 6900 Main St., Stratford, Connecticut 06615 (hereinafter "SAC") and Air 
Ghislaine, Inc. 3800 Southern Blvd, West Palm Beach, Florida 33406 (hereinafter "Air Ghislaine") in 
connection with the support of Air Ghislaine's S-76C-H- helicopter(s). 
1.0 
DEFIjITIONS 
As used in this Agreement, the following terms have the meanings indicated: 
1A 
"Aircraft" means the S-76C-f-i- helicopter(s) owned and/or operated by Air Ghislaine. 
1B 
"WEB HELOTRAC" means the internet based Helotrac System that contains transcribed data and 
information from Chapter 4, Airworthiness Limitations, and Chapter 5, Inspection Requirements 
Information (including manufacturer/FAA scheduled inspections, time-limited components, and 
technical bulletins) from the S-76C++ helicopter support manuals customarily provided by SAC 
generally to its S-76C-H- helicopter customers. WEB HELOTRAC also includes any subsequent 
corrections, fixes, upgrades, revisions, enhancements, and/or modifications to WEB HELOTRAC 
that SAC provides generally to its S-76C-H- helicopter customers subscribing to WEB 
HELOTRAC. 
IC 
"Source Data" means preexisting data and information associated with the Aircraft that is provided 
by Air Ghislaine for incorporation in WEB HELOTRAC. Such Source Data, and may include, but 
is not limited to, logbook data and computer generated reports or files containing maintenance 
information for the Aircraft. 
ID 
"Operating Data" means data and information generated by Air Ghislaine during operation of the 
Aircraft that is entered into WEB HELOTRAC by Air Ghislaine. 
1E 
"Database" means airy files (data, text, graphics, as applicable) associated with WEB HELOTRAC. 
2.0 
ACCESS/SET-UP/TRAINING 
2A 
SAC has developed a recommended list of maintenance requirements with recommended 
frequencies for the Aircraft indicated hereon. 
Such schedule has been programmed into a 
computer to establish the product called WEB HELOTRAC, and this information shall be 
provided to the Operator after execution of this agreement through WEB HELOTRAC upon 
payment of the Annual Fee described in Attachment A. Upon payment, SAC shall provide access 
to WEB J-IELOTRAC. 
2B 
Upon signing this Agreement Air Ghislaine shall provide SAC with any Source Data for entry by 
SAC into WEB HELOTRAC within thirty (30) days along with an Entry of Source Data Fee 
described below. SAC shall input all Source Data into WEB ITELOTRAC within thirty (30) days 
of its date of receipt of Entry of Source Data Fee or the Source Data, whichever is later.

3A

license, without the right to sublicense, to use WEB FIELO FRAC on the Computer in support of

(data, text, as applicable) associated therewith, as required and the right to generate reports as

required; however, Air Ghislaine shall not export all or any portion of the files (data, text, graphic) 
associated with WEB HELOTRAC. Additionally, Air Ghislaine shall not modify, adapt, change, 
prepare derivative works based upon, or in any other manner alter any portion of WEB

WEB HELOTRAC without the prior written permission of SAC. 
3C 
Air Ghislaine agrees not to disassemble, decompile, reverse engineer, or in any other manner 
attempt to access or produce the source code of all or any portion of WEB HELOTRAC. 
3D 
Air Ghislaine shall provide SAC with updates on a recurring basis of Operational Data entered into 
WEB HELOTRAC by Air Ghislaine. Air Ghislaine hereby authorizes SAC to use any Source 
and/or Operational Data provided to SAC by Air Ghislaine pursuant to this Agreement in 
maintenance management or other studies relating to the maintenance support and/or operation of 
helicopter products and to distribute such studies to third parties as deemed appropriate by SAC in 
the conduct of its business.

ANALYST SERVICES 
10A

I 0C

I OD

10F

c. Maintenance Due List Report (report of projected scheduled maintenance)

10H. 
Air Ghislaine shall timely update compliance in the HELOTRAC System for both scheduled and

accomplished. 
101.

(software).

OPERATIONS 
LIEUTENANT 
A staff member must observe all inmates confined in a continuous locked down status, such as administrative 
detention or disciplinary segregation, at least once in the first 30 minute period of the hour (example, 12:00 
a.m. — 12:30 a.m.) followed by another round in the second 30 minutes period of the same ho r (example, 
12:30 am — 1:00 a.m.), thus ensuring an inmate is observed at least twice per hour. These rounds are to be 
conducted on an irregular schedule and no more than 40 minutes apart. All observations mulct be 
documented.

personnel in the cellblock until the arresting agent(s) make arrangements for the prisoner's initial appearance before a United States 
Magistrate. A prisoner remains the responsibility of the arresting agency until remanded to the custody of the USMS by the courts.

agency must be available to respond to the cellblock in order to address any issues with their prisoner (e.g., medical, disciplinary). If 
the arresting agency refuses to comply with USMS procedures, the courtesy hold may be refused. Meals are not provided by the 
USMS, and remain the responsibility of the arresting agent(s).
